note: Issue 278, institutional-contacts.md section 3. He asks for every duty to be set aside for the one month. The Author's second ruling took away the three-month announcement, so there is nothing scheduled here: the priest writes, the PC answers, and it starts - which is why the letter talks about a month already begun rather than one coming. The Author's third ruling is what the last body line is about: a resource under protest keeps its duty through either waiver, so a colony in protest does not get a holiday from the thing it is protesting. He does not know that, and the letter does not tell him; the PC finds out when the waiver does not reach it.

body.text: The holy day is upon us. I did not write earlier because there was nothing earlier to write about — it arrives when it arrives, and it has arrived.

What I am asking is that every duty be set aside for the month. All of them, on everything, across the colony. I know how that reads written down. It reads worse than it is: it is one month, and the month is nearly always a poor one for trade anyway, which I mention as an argument and not as a confession.

What I am asking is that every duty be set aside for the month. All of them, on everything, across the colony. I have stopped dressing these requests up, since it has never made any difference to the answer.
A colony that keeps the day together is a colony that has something in common besides a governor. I would not put it that way to the Crown. I am putting it that way to you.

I am told there are towns refusing the Crown's duty on this or that. I do not know what becomes of my request where a town has already stopped paying, and I confess I have not thought about it very hard. That is your arithmetic and not mine.
